To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glutamic dehydroganse from bovine liver can be dissociated to inactive subunits under a wide variety or conditions; reconstitution of active hexamers is not possible.
the dissociation of the enzyme is accompanied by irreversible side reactions and that the regain of fluorescence is not accompanied by reactivation.
glutamic dehydrogease from bovine livers can be dissociated to monomers under a wide variety or conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of the denaturation of glutamic dehydragenase, and with the characterization of the conformational states of the polypepide chain in various denaturants.
the elucidation of the mechanism of the dissociation and reconstitution of bovine liver glutamic dehydrogease in various denaturants.
the dissociation and the “renatulation” of bovine liver glutamic dehydrogenease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glutamic dehydroge-nase from bovine livers is not a protein that can be “denatured” and subsequently “renatured” under physiological conditions.
the monomeric polypeptide chain is not able to reorganize into a functional native conformation.
the monomeric subunit of glutamic dehydogenase does not possess the information to fold back to the native state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the “renatuation” of glutamic dehydogenase from bovine livers is a process of aggregation rather than of reconstitution.
the dissociated monomers of glutamic dehydogenase can be reconstituted into an active oligomer only if this process is not accompanied by the formation of inactive high molecular weight aggregates.
the monomerization of oligomeric proteins by various denaturants is not always accompanied by a complete loss of secondary structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reconstitution process is not only a function of the denaturating environment (e.g. 6 ᴘᴜᴀ, pH 1.5, pH 2.0) but also of the conditions applied for the renaturation (e.g. temperature, pH, pressure, concentration, additives).
denaturation is a reversible reaction, and that renaturation of proteins can be achieved under a wide variety or conditions.

, although the reconstitution of a protein from its dissociated subunits is a well-known process, the reconstitution of oligomeric enzymes is not a general rule, but depends on the specific structure of the protein under study.
